name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

prose.intro_html:
Here is a dinner that does the two things a busy week needs most: it feeds a crowd and it barely asks you to stand at the stove. No boiling a pot of pasta, no browning the chicken in batches, no separate sauce simmering while you stir. You blend, you dump, you bake. The oven does the cooking.

The trick that makes this one earn its place in the rotation is the sauce. Instead of a heavy cream base, we run cottage cheese and Boursin through a blender until it is silky and pourable, then thin it with chicken broth. That is where the protein comes from, and it is why one container lands at 54.8 grams of protein for 603 calories. Artichoke hearts, peas, and a hit of lemon keep it from feeling like a heavy casserole. It tastes bright. It just happens to be muscle food.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a short, honest grocery list. A few notes so you buy it right the first time.

  • Boursin comes in 5.2 oz packages. You need 12 oz for the full 14-serving batch, which is two and a third packages. That means grabbing three and having a little left over. Plan to use the odd bit on toast or fold it into scrambled eggs during the week so nothing sits in the fridge going to waste.
  • Buy the big tub of cottage cheese. You need 4 and 2/3 cups, which is a 2 lb 5 oz worth. The large tub covers it in one grab instead of juggling small cups.
  • Canned artichoke hearts, not marinated. You want the plain ones packed in water so you control the lemon and salt yourself. Drain them well and give them a rough chop.
  • Frozen peas are your friend here. They go into the casserole straight from the freezer, no thawing, and a bag keeps in the freezer far better than fresh peas keep in the crisper.
  • Grate your own parmesan off a block if you can. It melts into a better golden top than the shelf-stable shaker dust. You need 2 and 1/3 cups grated.
  • Two lemons cover both jobs. Zest them first, then juice them. You need the zest and the juice from the same fruit, so do not throw the peels away before you scrape them.
prose.make_it:
This is a dump-and-bake, so the whole method is really just build the sauce, layer the pan, and let the oven work.

  1. Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a large 9x13 casserole dish. At this batch size you may need a second dish or a deeper pan, so eyeball your volume before you commit.
  2. Blend the sauce. Into a blender or food processor go the cottage cheese, Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Run it until it is completely smooth, then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is silky. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right. That thin sauce is what cooks the pasta.
  3. Layer the pan. Spread the dry penne across the bottom. Scatter the raw cubed chicken, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Now pour the blended sauce over everything and make sure every bit of pasta is submerged. Dry pasta poking above the liquid will not cook, so push it down.
  4. Cover and bake. Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should be a touch undercooked at this point. Top with the grated parmesan and return it to the oven, uncovered, for another 5 to 10 minutes. Bump the heat up if you want the top to go golden. If the pasta already feels done when you stir it, just add the parmesan and move to resting.
  5. Rest before you serve. Let it sit at least 10 minutes out of the oven. This is not optional. The sauce sets and the pasta finishes drinking up the liquid while it rests. Then scatter the chopped parsley or basil over the top and serve.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers, and the honest way to split it even is to weigh it. Set your empty casserole dish on a kitchen scale before you cook and note the weight, or just weigh the finished dish and subtract what you know the empty pan weighs. Take the total weight of the food, divide by 14, and that is your target grams per container.

Then portion by the scale, not by the eyeball. A casserole like this hides its weight in the sauce, so a scoop that looks generous can be light. Weighing each container is the difference between 14 real servings at 603 calories and 54.8 grams of protein each, and ten big portions plus four sad ones. Let everything cool before you lid the containers so the tops do not steam and go soft.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters when you are cooking to a budget. This whole tray comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a full dinner with 54.8 grams of protein for less than most drive-thru value meals, and you are not eating standing over the sink at 9 p.m.

Cottage cheese is doing quiet, cheap work here. It carries the protein and the creamy body that a jar of alfredo would charge you double for, and it comes off the same shelf you already walk past.

head.description: A no-boil dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, and a blended cottage cheese sauce. 14 high-protein meal-prep servings at 603 calories and 54.8g protein each.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, high protein meal prep, chicken artichoke pasta, cottage cheese pasta bake, budget meal prep dinner, 14 servings
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a large 9x13 casserole dish.
Blend the cottage cheese, Boursin, minced garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then add the chicken broth and blend again until silky and thin.
Spread the dry penne in the dish, scatter the cubed raw chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over it, then pour the sauce over everything until the pasta is fully submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 40 minutes. Remove foil, stir, top with parmesan, and bake uncovered another 5 to 10 minutes until golden.
Rest at least 10 minutes, then top with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
